solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Informed about origin of dubious promotion on the web

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: someone informed is aware of the facts

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, so only the start of dubious is used

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable person comments on where a shady online advertisement came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that pushes advertising at a computer user is a form of promotion delivered online.

clue.text: Dead time after month full of enjoyment

indicators.note: after places the time letter behind everything else
full of says the month abbreviation holds the enjoyment within it

parts.note: DEC is the standard abbreviation for December
enjoyment is fun

explanation.surface: Life ends after a month of good times.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer existing or functioning is called dead, which is the sense of this word.

clue.text: Trouble about love?

definitions.note: the verb sense: to love dearly

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing
RE is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: Asking whether romance is just a lot of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to love them intensely, a near synonym; the question mark flags the verb.

clue.text: Alienated journalist swigging rum

indicators.note: swigging means drinking down, so the journalist takes the other piece inside

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
rum in British usage means odd or strange

explanation.surface: A hack drinking rum has become cut off from friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being swigged, but here it is the old British adjective meaning peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are estranged have been made distant or unfriendly, which is what alienated means.

clue.text: Money firm when invested in central heating

parts.note: firm means hard, solid

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the word for when goes into the heating abbreviation

parts.note: CH is the familiar abbreviation for central heating in British property adverts
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Advice that money becomes solid when it is put into home heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash in coins and notes rather than cheques or credit is hard currency, i.e. ready money.

clue.text: Shamefaced Government supporting party after swing

indicators.note: after puts the party and government pieces behind the swing word
in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so G goes below the party

parts.note: to hang is to swing, as from a rope
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A politician looks ashamed after the party swung behind the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is guilty and sheepish, exactly the expression of someone shamefaced.

clue.text: Runs one to check pin

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: A batsman's runs are scrutinised to hold the score in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal fastener hammered through to hold plates together works as a pin.

clue.text: Questions of a religious nature caught a chemist out

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pharmacist is dismissed in cricket, caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a series of set questions and answers teaching Christian doctrine.

clue.text: Operator performing under sudden influx

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the performing word beneath the influx word

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush or influx
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Someone works while coping with a sudden rush of patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations, so is literally an operator.

clue.text: Elector not sure to be forgiven a lot, possibly including treason without cause

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: without means take the cause word away, leaving one letter of treason

parts.note: taken as written
a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: An undecided voter might be pardoned many things, even treason with no motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treason without cause' leaves just T, which 'including' adds to FORGIVENALOT before 'possibly' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter not committed to any party, who may swing either way at an election, is an elector not yet sure.

clue.text: Available when needed, but moaned about empty neighbourhood

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters of moaned are rearranged
empty means the inside of neighbourhood is removed, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled about a deserted part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: MOANED rearranged gives ONDEMA; 'empty' strips neighbourhood to ND.
explanation.definitionFit: A service supplied whenever someone asks for it, such as streamed television, is provided at request.

clue.text: Fixed with diplomatic handling, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people diplomatically

explanation.surface: A problem was sorted out through careful diplomacy, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack something is to fasten it with small nails or loose stitches, so it is fixed.

clue.text: What may tie up call on the way?

parts.note: ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way or road
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Wondering what could hold up a visit made on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the call after the way piece in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cord used to bind parcels is the obvious thing for tying things up.

clue.text: Comprehensive is undecided, with no study

indicators.note: with no tells us the study word is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an inconclusive result leaves the matter undecided
to con is an old word for to study or learn

explanation.surface: A remark that a comprehensive school is indecisive and does no studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests the British state school, but it is the adjective meaning all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that includes everything is all-embracing, the sense of comprehensive here.

clue.text: Poles given to eating nuts and flowers

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of eating go wild

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people like to snack on nuts and flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality, but it is the two magnetic poles; 'given to' just attaches them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are mountain plants known for their deep blue trumpet blooms.

clue.text: Plant caught, surrounded by angry Russians

indicators.note: surrounded by means the caught letter sits inside the other piece
angry suggests agitation, so the letters of Russians are churned

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A spy planted in Moscow is caught and ringed by furious locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' tempts as a spy, but it is the flower; RUSSIANS rearranged round C gives the bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcissus, including daffodils, is a spring-flowering bulb plant.

clue.text: Monitor lively chat by women and follow

indicators.note: lively suggests movement, so the letters of chat are stirred

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on spirited gossip among women and trailing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog body oversees an industry, so it acts as a monitor.

clue.text: Good-humoured sailor in a 4 x 440 yds

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the distance

parts.note: four times 440 yards is 1760 yards, one mile
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the stock crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A cheerful seaman runs in a relay race of four laps.
explanation.walkthrough: '4 x 440 yds' looks like a relay, but it is just a sum: 1760 yards is one mile.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and pleasant in manner, an amiable person is good-humoured.

clue.text: Allocate a position to person with BSc, but without university

indicators.note: without means the university letter is taken out

parts.note: someone holding a BSc degree is a graduate

explanation.surface: Giving a job to a science graduate who never went to university.
explanation.definitionFit: To gradate is to arrange in grades or steps, assigning each a position on a scale.

clue.text: Careless young lady attached to soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a stock crossword unit of soldiers
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A careless girl gets involved with troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young lady' tempts as the definition, but 'Careless' at the start defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remiss means negligent in one's duty, which is careless.

clue.text: Tighten up, seeing nurse welcome spat

indicators.note: welcome means take in, so the nurse holds the quarrel

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, is an old British nursing grade
a spat is a petty quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: A nurse tenses up as a quarrel arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen is to make or become rigid and tense, to tighten up.

clue.text: Cut dead awkward Luddite ignoring theologian

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters that remain are jumbled
ignoring means leaving the theologian's letters out

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree

explanation.surface: A clumsy anti-technology campaigner snubs a clergyman completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut dead' reads as a snub, but 'dead' gives D; LUDDITE without DD leaves LUITE, made into ILUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a drink is to cut it with water, weakening its strength.

clue.text: Bush makes appearance in newsreel, derided

indicators.note: makes appearance in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A President Bush shows up in a news clip and is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the US president, but it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or small tree bearing white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Area island group use up creating pollution

parts.note: CI is the Channel Islands, a group off the French coast
to drain is to use up or exhaust

explanation.surface: Over-use of resources on an archipelago creates environmental damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain made acidic by sulphur and nitrogen emissions is a well-known type of pollution.

clue.text: Three minutes' boxing gets you shot

definitions.meaning: a boxing bout is split into three-minute sessions of fighting
a single bullet or shell fired is a single piece of ammunition, as in firing off a single discharge

explanation.surface: A bout of boxing lasting three minutes leaves you shot.
explanation.definitionFit: One period of a boxing bout and a single discharge of ammunition share this word.

clue.text: Screen worker's nude game?

parts.note: a blind is a window screen
a man is a worker, as in management and men; the possessive gives the S
in the buff means naked

explanation.surface: A naked worker behind a screen might be up for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the comic picture of a naked worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game in which a blindfolded player tries to catch the others.

clue.text: Practise, seeing Shearer troubled before Newcastle's final

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of Shearer are reordered
final means the last letter of Newcastle is taken

explanation.surface: Football star Alan Shearer, agitated, trains before Newcastle's cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer was Newcastle United's star striker, which gives the surface its football picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play is to practise it before performance.

clue.text: Tracks I'd found in grass

definitions.note: plural in the clue but a single siding is a short side track, often a set of rails

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the grass word

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing to police, as is to sing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that one discovered rail lines among the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A short railway line off the main line, where trains are parked, is a siding.
